newsitem.title: PERU: Peru rebels could hold 490 hostages - letter.
newsitem.headline: Peru rebels could hold 490 hostages - letter.

text.p: Peruvian guerrillas could be holding as many as 490 hostages at the Japanese ambassador's home in Lima, according to a letter faxed from within the residence to hostages' relatives.

The fax was signed by Peruvian Foreign Minister Francisco Tudela, Japanese ambassador Morihisa Aoki and other ambassadors held in the building. It was distributed to journalists at the scene by Liliana Panizo, the wife of congressmen Javier Diez Canseco, one of the hostgages.
The signatories said they were speaking on behalf of "around 490 people, Peruvian citizens and officials, and foreign functionaries and diplomats..."
Previous estimates by the government, released hostages and the guerrillas themselves had put the number of captives between 200 and 300.
"We believe it is indispensable to establish a dialogue," the letter read. "There are injured who require treatment."

Among the hostages were two Peruvian government ministers and at least 12 ambassadors from Asia, Latin America and Europe. Without setting a deadline, the rebels have threatened to kill all the hostages if the government does not release an estimated 400 to 500 MRTA prisoners and transport them to the jungle.
